# Abstract

This gazetteer documents WGS84 coordinates, indigenous and Norse toponymy, attested chronological spans and benchmark populations for 982 pre-modern settlements across Northern Canada and Greenland (`5,04M km²`) between `10000BC` and `1600AD`. Entries span from `6500BC` Mackenzie Dene occupation at Fisherman Lake (`120` peak) and `2400BC` Palaeo-Inuit coastal stations at Qeqertasussuk (`160` peak), Independence I (`50`) and Sermermiut (`480`) to classic Dorset and Thule whaling complexes at Qariaraqyuk (`480` and `380`), Alarnerk (`380`), Igloolik (`360`), Sadlermiut (`340`), Kuukpak (`580`) and Kittigazuit (`1k`), alongside mediaeval Norse estate centres at Brattahlíð (`620` peak) and Garðar (`450`). All `982` settlements in the gazetteer carry CENTAUR provenance and reconcile cleanly against `1.110` source-ledger candidates alongside 128 consolidated duplicate-alias entries.

# Background

High-latitude settlement visibility concentrates where seasonal marine-mammal harvests, caribou water crossings or Norse fjord pastures anchored multi-family winter dwellings [@mcghee1996; @friesen2016]. In the Mackenzie Delta and Coronation Gulf, driftwood-framed semi-subterranean winter houses at Kittigazuit and Kuukpak supported large beluga-hunting aggregations [@morrison1990]. Across the eastern archipelago, whalebone winter houses at Qariaraqyuk and Foxe Basin polynya middens at Alarnerk and Igloolik anchored Dorset and Thule networks [@savelle2002; @maxwell1985; @taylor1968]. In West and East Greenland, *Nunniffiit* heritage inventories supplement excavated Norse turf-and-stone farmsteads around Tunulliarfik and Igaliku fjords and Disko Bay Saqqaq and Kalaallit stations [@arneborg2012; @gronnow2004; @mathiassen1933].

# Methodology

Sites enter the source ledger when archaeological house-pit surveys, national heritage registers or mediaeval Norse farm inventories establish bounded coordinates and residential population trajectories [@lynnerup1998; @savelle2002]. Across Greenland, overlapping *Nunniffiit* coordinate twins within `2 km` or identical centroids (`128` entries) are consolidated as duplicate aliases so each locality is subtracted only once from sub-regional rural weights. Dispersed boreal hunting stations without fixed house structures remain represented in the rural kriging surface [@gordon1996]. Table \ref{tab:summary} summarises included counts and summed site peaks across the five divisions.

# Testing and Validation

Schema and ledger checks confirm `982` included settlements, `128` excluded duplicate-alias records (`1.110` total candidates), `0` unaccounted candidates and `0` coordinate errors (`60,09` to `83,20` N and `16,42` to `134,23` W). Every record carries CENTAUR provenance. Figure \ref{fig:settlements} charts the rank-size hierarchy across the `982` catalogued sites led by Kittigazuit (`1k`).

## Sub-Regional Settlement Summaries

West Greenland (`731` records) spans Disko Bay Palaeo-Inuit and Kalaallit occupation at Qeqertasussuk (`160` peak), Saqqaq (`190`) and Sermermiut (`480` in `1600AD`), coastal Thule centres at Kangeq (`320`), Comer's Midden (`310`), Nuulliit (`290`), Kangamiut (`270`) and Illorpaat (`240`), alongside mediaeval Norse Eastern Settlement hubs at Brattahlíð (`620` peak) and Garðar (`450`) [@gronnow2004; @arneborg2012; @lynnerup1998]. East and High North Greenland (`205` records) combines early Independence I campsites (`50` peak) with Tunumiit and Thule coastal stations at Skjoldungen (`160`), Clavering Island (`160`) and Scoresbysund (`140`) [@mathiassen1933; @friesen2016].

In the Eastern and High Arctic (`29` records), Somerset Island's Qariaraqyuk (`480` and `380` clusters) and Foxe Basin polynya towns at Alarnerk (`380`) and Igloolik (`360`) pair with Sadlermiut (`340`), Cumberland Sound (`310`), Naujan (`310`) and Lake Harbour (`260`) [@savelle2002; @maxwell1985; @taylor1968]. Across the Central and Western Arctic (`13` records), Kittigazuit (`1k` in `1600AD`) and Kuukpak (`580`) anchor Mackenzie Delta beluga harvesting alongside Nuvugak (`320`), Lady Franklin Point (`310`), Ekalluk River (`260`) and Bloody Falls (`180`) [@morrison1990; @nash1969], while the Mackenzie Dene subarctic (`4` records) is led by Deline on Great Bear Lake (`260` peak), Taltheilei Narrows (`160`), Trout Lake (`150`) and Fisherman Lake (`120`) [@gordon1996].

# Limitations

Small summer tent-ring camps across interior Barrenlands, Victoria Island and Northeast Greenland lack multi-family winter middens and remain absorbed in the rural kriging background, while comprehensive *Nunniffiit* heritage registration makes Greenland far denser in point count (`936` records combined) than the Canadian boreal shield and central Arctic islands (`46` records) [@friesen2016; @gordon1996].
